_notes: Taito do Brasil 1979 hardware (PinMAME taito_old). Compiled 2026-10 by evilwraith from the Shock ROM, three saved
images (attract, mid-game at ball 3, after the match sequence) and a live Shock game on an AtGames ALP4K that
read back 50,551 and three credits through ScoreServer. The window is at 0x1000: display at 0x1000, command DMA
at 0x1010, settings 0x10F0-0x10F8, high score 0x10F9, credits 0x10FF with its display copy at 0x100F. obaobao
(Oba-Oba on this hardware) references every declared address identically; no image yet. Football's ROM is lost.
Display scores are three BCD bytes least-significant first (platform endian: little); 0xFF 0xFF 0xFF is a blank
display. The nine-byte BCD settings block is edited from the service menu and validated at reset (a non-BCD byte
restores all nine from ROM); its nine entries are identified from the Shock operator sheet (see adjustments).
No checksum. The firmware deliberately resumes a game in progress at reset; PinMAME's taito driver (2026-10)
marks the saved game over on load so a table starts in attract.

player_count._notes: 1 in all three images and throughout the live game; the reset path refuses to resume with 5 or more.
player_count.label: Players

current_player._notes: One bit per player - 1, 2, 4, 8 for players one to four, 0 in attract - which the values list turns into the player number. The firmware finds the number by rotating the byte right until the carry sets and compares it with the player count (Shock 0x0CBE). Reads 1 through a one-player Shock game (live); the multi-player values are from the code, and Oba-Oba runs the same routine against 0x409E and reads 1, 2, 4, 8 live.
current_player.label: Current Player

credits._notes: Stored value; the firmware keeps a display copy at 0x100F.
credits.label: Credits

match._notes: Match digit shown after the game; cycles 0-9 during play (the randomiser).
match.label: Match

game_over._notes: Bit 0 of the firmware's flags byte: set in attract and by its reset path when it declines to resume, clear during a game.
game_over.label: Game Over

tilted._notes: Bit 1 of the flags byte: set at a tilt on ball 1 and cleared when the next ball started (live).
tilted.label: Tilted

score._notes: Most-significant byte first, unlike the display; the reset path reloads it from the ROM's minimum if it reads lower.

01._notes: Labels and ranges from the Shock operator sheet (backport/Manuals/Taito_Brazil_Shock_Dip_Switch_Info.jpg); byte positions and defaults match every image captured. Defaults are each set's own factory table, read from its ROM (the ten bytes the reset path copies in when a settings byte is not BCD).
01.label: Balls Per Game

02._notes: 'Fichas/Partida' (Cosmic: 'Credito/Partida'). A two-digit code, not a count: the sheets allow 11-14 and list 15 as a forbidden value that forces the default. What the digits mean is not stated on either sheet.
02.label: Coinage (code)

03._notes: 'Credito/Maximo'. The firmware clamps the stored credits to this value at boot.
03.label: Maximum Credits

04._notes: 'Incentivo'; the sheet allows 01 and 11-14. The 1980 games (drakor, meteort) hold 04 here, outside that set, so its meaning on those is not confirmed. No default is declared: the factory value differs between the sets this map covers (obaobao 04, shock 01).
04.label: Incentive

05._notes: '1o Score'. Shown x10,000 (the map's scale; min/max are in those units, as upstream does). One BCD byte compared against the two most-significant digits of the score (x10,000); the same routine in every set.
05.label: Replay Level 1

06._notes: Shown x10,000. '2o Score'. Annulled when equal to adjustment 5 (the sheet says so, and the routine skips it).
06.label: Replay Level 2

07._notes: Named from the Shock and Cosmic operator sheets. The firmware compares the score with this level and, unless it equals replay level 2, jumps to a per-game hook; the hook does something game-specific on shock, obaobao. Read from each ROM's code.
07.label: Extra Ball Score

09._notes: 'Credito/Record': credits awarded for beating the high score.
09.label: Credits For High Score
